source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 11: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
Denominator mein ek linear factor \(x - 1\) hai aur ek quadratic factor \(x^2 + 1\) jo real numbers mein toot nahi sakta (irreducible). Yeh Case-III hai.
Quadratic factor ke upar sirf constant nahi, balke linear numerator \(Bx + C\) likhna parta hai.
Plan: \(x = 1\) rakh kar \(A\), phir coefficients compare kar ke \(B\) aur \(C\); integral mein \(\ln\) aur \(\tan^{-1}\) aayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{x^2 + 2x - 1}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 1)}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: yeh integral.
Tareeqa: partial fractions, Case-III. \(x^2 + 1\) kabhi zero nahi hota (kyunke \(x^2 \ge 0\)), is liye is ka koi real root nahi aur yeh linear factors mein nahi tootta.

Partial fractions likhein
\[\dfrac{x^2 + 2x - 1}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 1)} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{Bx + C}{x^2 + 1}\]
\[x^2 + 2x - 1 = A(x^2 + 1) + (Bx + C)(x - 1) \quad (1)\]
Kyun: Rule yeh hai ke numerator ki degree denominator se ek kam ho sakti hai. Linear factor ke upar constant (degree 0), quadratic factor ke upar linear \(Bx + C\) (degree 1). Agar sirf \(B\) likhein to har case poora nahi hoga.

(1) mein \(x = 1\) rakhein
\[1 + 2 - 1 = A(2)\]
\[A = 1\]
Kyun: \(x = 1\) par \(x - 1 = 0\), is liye \((Bx + C)(x - 1)\) wala poora term zero. \(x^2 + 1\) ka real root nahi, is liye \(B\), \(C\) ke liye yeh shortcut nahi chalega.

Coefficients compare karein
\[x^2:\ 1 = A + B,\ B = 0\]
\[\text{constant}:\ -1 = A - C,\ C = 2\]
Kyun: \((Bx + C)(x - 1) = Bx^2 + (C - B)x - C\) aur \(A(x^2 + 1) = Ax^2 + A\). \(x^2\) ka coefficient: \(A + B = 1\); constant: \(A - C = -1\). Teesri equation (\(x\) ka coefficient) \(C - B = 2\) se tasdeeq bhi ho gayi.

Integral lein
\[\int \left(\dfrac{1}{x - 1} + \dfrac{2}{x^2 + 1}\right)dx\]
\[= \ln|x - 1| + 2\tan^{-1} x + c\]
Kyun: \(B = 0\) hone se quadratic wala hissa sirf \(\frac{2}{x^2 + 1}\) reh gaya, aur \(\int \frac{dx}{1 + x^2} = \tan^{-1} x\) jaana pehchana formula hai (kyunke \(\frac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1} x = \frac{1}{1 + x^2}\)).

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{1}{x - 1} + \dfrac{2}{x^2 + 1} = \dfrac{x^2 + 1 + 2x - 2}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{x^2 + 2x - 1}{(x - 1)(x^2 + 1)} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Dono fractions ko wapas jama kiya to asal integrand mil gaya, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.text: Kitab ke aakhir mein answers (page 302) mein Exercise 3.4 ke jawab ghalat heading "Exercise 3.6" ke neeche chhape hain. Is sawal ka jawab us block ka item (xi) hai: \(\ln|x - 1| + 2\tan^{-1} x + c\). Yeh jawab sahi hai. Jis block par "Exercise 3.4" likha hai (page 301) woh kisi aur exercise ke jawab hain, is liye wahan se milane ki koshish na karein.
